values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/carneylake ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Carney Lake State Forest Campground: nightly fee $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boat launch on Carney Lake. ORVs may run between the campground and nearby trails (designated ORV road).

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/carneylake ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (boat ramp/carry-in column), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/carneylake ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 16 'tent and small trailer sites' (agency wording, no length limit posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/carneylake + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Carney Lake State Forest Campground: 16 campsites; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site'), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground on the shore of Carney Lake, Dickinson County, 14 mi NE of Iron Mountain via M-95 and Carney Lake Rd; managed by Bewabic State Park. Walleye, panfish and pike; hiking, and ORV-trail access by a designated ORV road. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 16 tent/small-trailer sites, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, boat launch, first-come only (confirmed), 15-day max (now on the entry). Season May 1 - Oct 31 (already manual, the table's Nov 1 - May 1 closure). Phone differs (flag). No closure notice. Note trimmed of field restatements.
